purpose: Show a founder or CTO, before they share anything, how Alliance AI Partners handles partner data: it stays in their systems wherever possible, we take only the access a job needs, a person reviews every piece of work, and a national privacy law stands behind it.

seo.title: Data and security | Alliance AI Partners
seo.description: How Alliance AI Partners handles your data: it stays in your systems wherever possible, we take only the access a job needs, and a person reviews every piece of work.

sections.name: Section · Hero
sections.job: Say the promise in four words and show least access as a concrete, sample access record.
sections.desktop: Text left: Display/XL title with one regular-weight accent, Body/LG lead, Secondary button and a link, a caption that the full data policy comes before launch. Right: a framed product visual, a sample 'Access record' card (lock icons, mono access levels) with a smaller 'Reviewed by a person' card overlapping its lower left. No Primary in the hero; the closing band carries it.
sections.mobile: Title, lead, full-width Secondary, link, caption; the access record card follows at full width with the review card overlapping its foot.

content.heading: Your data stays yours.
content.lead: It stays in your systems wherever possible. We take only the access a job needs, and a person on our team reviews every piece of work before it reaches you.
body: We will publish our full data policy on this page before launch.

items.title: Your help desk
items.text: Drafts replies; a person sends them

items.title: Shared drive
items.text: One folder for the check-up files

items.title: Access ends when the job ends.

ctas.label: See the AI tools we use

images.source: UI composition drawn in Figma: a white 'Access record' card marked Sample, three systems with lock icons and mono access levels, a footer row 'Access ends when the job ends. Ends [date]', and an overlapping 'Reviewed by a person [Name], [Role]' card.
images.placement: right half of the hero (desktop); under the caption (mobile)
images.alt: Sample access record: read-only access to a CRM, draft-only access to a help desk, one shared folder, ending when the job ends.

sections.name: Section · Four rules
sections.job: Spell out the four rules that apply to every project.
sections.desktop: Asymmetric section head; bento with one large card (an inset diagram of 'Your systems' tags with 'Our team works here', and a dashed 'A copy: only if you decide' box, then Heading/3 and text) and three stacked cards on the right with service icons and Heading/4 titles.
sections.mobile: Head, the large card, then the three cards stacked.

content.heading: Four rules on every project.
content.lead: They hold for every service we offer, from the AI check-up to a developer working inside your team.

items.title: Your data stays in your systems wherever possible.
items.text: We work inside your tools and accounts instead of copying your data into ours. When a job does need a copy, you decide first.

items.title: We take only the access a job needs.
items.text: Named accounts, the lowest access level that does the work, removed when the job ends.

items.title: A person reviews every piece of work.
items.text: AI drafts and checks. A person on our team reviews the result before it reaches you or your customers.

items.title: Your data trains only what you own.
items.text: Your data is never used to train anything you don't own.

images.source: UI composition drawn in Figma inside the large bento card: a 'Your systems' panel with CRM, Help desk, Shared drive and Code tags and a 10% cyan-tinted 'Our team works here' row, beside a dashed 'A copy: only if you decide' box.
images.placement: top of the large bento card
images.alt: Diagram: our team works inside your systems; a copy is made only if you decide.

sections.name: Section · What we touch
sections.job: Show where each kind of data lives and who can see it, marked as a placeholder until the data policy is published.
sections.desktop: Section head, an Info alert, then a five-column table. Every cell is a bracketed placeholder.
sections.mobile: The table becomes stacked rows: one block per kind of data with four label and value lines.

content.heading: What we touch, and where it lives.
content.lead: Our data policy will list every kind of data we handle. Until it is published, this table shows what each row will tell you.
body: Alert (Info): Placeholder until the data policy is published. Each row below is filled in from the policy before launch.

sections.name: Section · Law band
sections.job: Name the Philippine privacy law and its independent regulator, with the source.
sections.desktop: Full-bleed 1440x640 band with the image behind a navy scrim; text block on the right: Display/LG title with one cyan accent, Body/LG with Source key 1, a cyan link to the Act, and the mono source line below a hairline.
sections.mobile: 390x760 band, scrim from the top, text and source at the top.

content.heading: Our promise, backed by law.
content.lead: Alliance AI Partners is based in the Philippines. Personal data there is protected by the Data Privacy Act of 2012, enforced by an independent National Privacy Commission.

sources.text: Republic Act No. 10173, the Data Privacy Act of 2012. Supreme Court of the Philippines E-Library. Retrieved 2026-11-02.

images.aspectMobile: 390x760, crop to the lower left leaves
images.placement: background behind a navy scrim (behind the text on the right on desktop, from the top on mobile)

sections.name: Section · AI providers
sections.job: Say that every AI provider and tool that may touch partner data is published, and link to the subprocessor list.
sections.desktop: Split: text left (Heading/2, Body/LG, the change notice, Secondary button); right a framed preview of the subprocessor list (white card, placeholder rows, mono 'Last updated' and preview note).
sections.mobile: Text, then the preview card at full width, then a full-width Secondary button.

content.heading: Which AI tools touch your data.
content.lead: Some work runs through AI models and tools from other companies. We publish each one that may touch partner data: what it does, what it sees and where it runs.
body: Before a new provider touches your data, we tell you [notice period] ahead.
Preview. The full list is published before launch.

images.source: UI composition drawn in Figma: a white 'Subprocessors' card with a mono 'Last updated [date]' line, three placeholder rows and a mono preview note.

sections.name: Section · Security contact
sections.job: Give the security contact and the response promise in one strip.
sections.desktop: One wide white card: a lock icon in a Neutral 50 well, Heading/3 and text, and on the right the security address as an underlined link with a link to the disclosure policy.
sections.mobile: The card stacks: icon, title, text, address, link.

content.heading: Found a security problem?
content.lead: Tell us privately first. We acknowledge every report within [two working days].

sections.name: Section · Closing CTA
sections.job: Close with the AI check-up and what a partner gets from it.
sections.desktop: Navy chapter: Ribbon rule (the page's one ribbon signature), Display/LG title with a cyan accent, lead, the page's one Primary and a cyan link; on the right three hairline rows with cyan check icons.
sections.mobile: Rule, title, lead, the three rows, full-width Primary, link.

content.heading: Start with an AI check-up.
content.lead: A short first project, and the easiest way to start.

items.title: We learn how your business works.
We find where AI could save you time or money.
You get a plan with a fixed quote.

notes: Frames 38:45 and 39:1228 were built by a stopped duplicate builder and kept after review: lint clean on 2026-11-03 after two fixes (the law band Source key text raised from 10 to 12 px, and the fourth rule retitled 'Your data trains only what you own.' to match Brand DNA, since custom model training on a partner's own data is a listed service). Footer-linked trust page, so no nav item is current. The security-governance and lock visuals are used small and in context (lock icons on the access record and in the security strip, the shield service icon in the rules), never as padlock clip art. Everything that depends on the unpublished data policy is a bracketed placeholder and labelled as one (Brand DNA, Notes before launch 6). The only number shown (the Act and its year) carries Source key 1 and a dated source line.
